To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a transgenic mouse model of c9ALS/FTD expressing poly-PR shows motor dysfunction, loss of lower motor neurons, loss of Purkinge neurons, and brain weight loss, and that poly-PR is toxic in vivo.
we generate a transgene expressing poly-PR, which shows a role of poly-PR in the neurodegeneration and motor dysfunction in a mouse model.
we have generated a transgenic mouse model expressing poly-PR specifically in the neurons, and that these mice display motor dysfunction and neurodegenerative changes in the brain and spinal cord.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of a transgenic mouse expressing GFP-PR28 and its use in the study of poly-PR toxicity.
the study of the pathophysiology of neurodegenerative diseases and, more specifically, the mechanisms underlying motor neuron degeneration and neurodegeneration.
understanding the mechanisms of neurodegeneration in c9FTD and ALS, and the development of therapeutic interventions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transgenic mouse model generated in this study partly recapitulates some features of c9ALS/FTD and that these features are likely to be mediated by poly-PR.
the GFP-PR28 mouse model of C9ORF72 ALS/FTD partially models the disease, and that poly-PR plays a role in neurodegeneration.
our findings show that GFP-P28R transgenic mice partly models neuropathological features and motor dysfunction of c9FTL/ALS, and shows a role for poly-P28R in neurodegeneration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have generated a transgenic mouse model expressing GFP-PR28, a poly-PR DPR, and that this mouse line shows neurodegeneration in the cerebellar and spinal cord, and that this neurodegeneration is associated with transcriptional changes in the cerebellal transcriptome.
poly-PR is neurotoxic and can cause neurodegeneration.
we show the generation and characterization of a transgenic mouse model that expresses poly- PR, a DPR that is associated with the most common genetic form of ALS and frontotemporial dementia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show for the first time that a transgenic mouse model expressing poly-PR recapitulate the motor and neuropathological features observed in c9FTD and c9ALS patients.
we show that a mouse model of poly-PR can be used to model c9FTD and ALS, and that this model can help to understand the role of PR in neurodegeneration.
we have generated a mouse model that expresses poly- PR in neurons and that this mouse line shows motor dysfunction, neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation.
